user.title: BLE IRK Extractor Setup
user.description: Choose whether to configure BlueZ file paths to scan for existing IRKs, or pair a new Bluetooth device directly to extract its IRK.

paths.title: Configure BlueZ Paths
paths.description: Point the integration at the BlueZ bond data on your Home Assistant host. {path_help}

data_description.name: Friendly name for this extractor.
data_description.copied_path: Folder containing BlueZ info files copied into Home Assistant. Default: /config/bluez_irks.
data_description.host_path: BlueZ host storage. Default: /var/lib/bluetooth. Leave blank if this path is not available in the container.
data_description.scan_interval: How often to reread the BlueZ files, in minutes.

no_keys.title: No IRKs found yet
no_keys.description: The configured paths exist, but no Identity Resolving Keys were found in: {paths}. You can finish setup now and add keys later, or go back and correct the paths.

data_description.setup_anyway: Finish setup even though no keys are present yet. The sensor will update automatically when keys appear.

pair_device.title: Pair a new Bluetooth device
pair_device.description: Select the Bluetooth adapter you want to pair through ({adapter_count} available). Make sure the device is discoverable.

data_description.adapter_address: The host Bluetooth adapter to scan and pair through.

device_selection.title: Select a Bluetooth device
device_selection.description: Choose the device you want to pair with from the discovered list. This scan lasts up to {start_timeout} seconds.

pair_confirm.title: Confirm pairing
pair_confirm.description: You are about to pair with: {device_name} ({device_address}). Ensure the device is in pairing mode.

data_description.confirm: Start pairing and extract the device's IRK.

pairing_result.title: Pairing complete
pairing_result.description: The pairing with {device_name} ({device_address}) finished. Extracted IRK: {irk}. You can use it to set up Home Assistant's Private BLE Device integration.

data_description.create_pbd: Initiate the Private BLE Device setup with this IRK.

pairing_failed.title: Pairing Failed
pairing_failed.description: Could not pair automatically with {device_name} ({device_address}). iOS and other secure devices require pairing via the host BlueZ agent (bluetoothctl). Choose how you would like to proceed:

data_description.recovery_action: Choose whether to retry device discovery or switch to BlueZ host storage extraction.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure BLE IRK Extractor
reconfigure.description: Update the BlueZ source paths or scan interval. {path_help}

data_description.name: Friendly name for this extractor.
data_description.copied_path: Folder containing BlueZ info files copied into Home Assistant. Default: /config/bluez_irks.
data_description.host_path: BlueZ host storage. Default: /var/lib/bluetooth. Leave blank if this path is not available in the container.
data_description.scan_interval: How often to reread the BlueZ files, in minutes.

error.no_paths: Enter at least one BlueZ source path.
error.path_not_found: None of the configured paths exist. Check the paths and try again.
error.no_adapters: No Bluetooth adapters found. Enable Bluetooth in Home Assistant first.
error.no_devices_found: No discoverable devices found. Make sure the device is in pairing mode and try again.
error.pairing_failed: Pairing failed. Try pairing manually in Home Assistant's Bluetooth settings, then rescan.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: BLE IRK Extractor is already configured.
abort.no_pending_setup: The setup data was lost. Please start again.
abort.unknown_entry: The config entry could not be found.
abort.pbd_flow_started: Private BLE Device setup started with the extracted IRK.
abort.setup_completed: Setup completed. The sensor will now show the extracted IRK.
